summary: On-demand session-slice export: timezone-normalized, per-record pseudonymization salt + signed delivery receipts for regulatory review
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Citrine Bank, enterprise) requests an on-demand export of 'session-slices' for a narrow time window (2026-02-28 00:00:00 UTC to 2026-03-01 00:00:00 UTC) to support a regulatory review. Requirements: (1) per-record pseudonymization using a provided salt (HMAC-SHA256) that the customer can verify, (2) canonical timezone normalization to CET with original timestamps preserved in a separate field, (3) a signed delivery receipt (per-batch and per-file) that includes SHA256 checksums and a server-signed timestamp for chain-of-custody, (4) inclusion of minimal attribution fields (tenant_id, session_id, event_type) and suppression of other PII fields, and (5) replayable resume tokens so customer can resume an interrupted ingest.

Impact:
Customer needs this for an upcoming external audit with a hard deadline next week. Audit team will reject incomplete evidence. Late delivery risks contractual penalties.

Environment:
Production export from eu-west tenant partition for Citrine Bank (customer_id: citrine-001). Data volume estimate: ~1.2M events, expected export size ~3.1GB compressed.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- HMAC salt (base64) via secure support attachment (we received ephemeral note in support portal).
- Preferred delivery: presigned S3 put to their staging bucket (eu-west-1) and an optional Kafka mirror to their Event Hubs bridge for replay verification.

Requested output format:
- GZIP'd ndjson files named session-slice-<start>-<end>-part-<n>.ndjson.gz
- Each record: flat JSON with fields: record_id, tenant_id, session_id, event_type, ts_canonical_cet, ts_original_utc, pseudonymized_user_id, payload_hash, redact_fields:[]
- Manifest JSON including per-file SHA256 and aggregated HMAC over file list signed by Redwood CI key.

Customer expectations and acceptance criteria:
- They can verify per-record pseudonymization by reproducing HMAC with provided salt and comparing the pseudonymized_user_id field.
- Checksums must match, and signed receipt must be verifiable.
- Timezone canonicalization must be CET with original UTC retained.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Identify tenant partition citrine-001 and time window 2026-02-28T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z.
2) Run export job with field allowlist and redaction function using provided salt.
3) Generate per-file SHA256 and manifest, sign manifest with repo infra key.
4) Deliver to customer's presigned S3 and notify with delivery receipt.
logs:
Export job logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/export/2026-03-10/citrine-001/attempt-1
Sample file: s3://redwood-support-temp/citrine/session-slice-sample.ndjson.gz
Manifest (staging): https://drive.redwood/internal/manifests/manifest-20260310-staging.json
investigation_notes:
- Salt ingestion: header omitted in support upload flow -> fallback to platform salt.
- Signing: job routed to 'staging-sign' worker pool due to routing tag; needs policy fix.
- Resume token encoding changed in commit 7f9b2d0; customer expects base64url.
- PKI: RFC3161 stamping required; security team queued.
comments:
Maya Singh: Customer will provide S3 presigned bucket and confirmed compliance window.
Ethan Collins: Will implement shim for token compatibility and re-run.
Priya Rao (Security): PKI will prioritize; expect signed manifest within 24-36h.
resolution: Partial workaround delivered (sample). Full resolution pending: re-run export with customer salt, production signing (RFC3161), and resume-token compatibility fix. Target delivery 2026-03-14.
